notes: The study identifies spatially and temporally linked paired metamorphism in the Western Dharwar Craton (WDC) at the Archean-Proterozoic boundary (c. 2.53-2.41 Ga).
Paired metamorphism involves two adjacent metamorphic belts of the same age showing contrasting thermal gradients, such as high P/T versus low P/T regimes.
In the Early Earth, paired metamorphism is recognized by the duality of intermediate T/P (eclogite-HP granulite) and high T/P (granulite-UHT) regimes.
The medium-grade (MG) domain in the WDC features pelitic schists in the kyanite stability field with a maximum temperature (Tmax) of 630-650°C.
MG rocks followed clockwise P-T paths representing 'pulsating orogenesis,' involving multiple short-lived burial-exhumation and heating-cooling cycles.
The MG domain exhibits short-lived lower-crustal residence (10-20 Myrs) and relatively fast exhumation rates of 0.6-2 mm/yr.
The high-grade (HG) domain consists of mafic and metasedimentary granulites in the sillimanite stability field with a Tmax of 800-870°C.
HG rocks record a monocyclic clockwise P-T path with high T/P ratios, indicating a single prograde heating event.
The HG domain is characterized by extremely long-lived crustal residence (~238 Myrs) and ultra-slow cooling rates of approximately 2°C/Myr.
Research methods used to reconstruct these histories include P-T-t path modeling, garnet-biotite diffusion chronometry, and monazite chemical dating.
The findings support the 'peel-back convergence' model, which differentiates between a Thickened Crustal Zone (TCZ) and a Peel-off Zone (PoZ).
The MG domain represents the intermediate T/P conditions of the TCZ, while the HG domain aligns with the high T/P conditions of the PoZ.
This paired metamorphism indicates a transition from Archean plume-driven vertical tectonics to asymmetric plate subduction.
The hotter Archean Earth inhibited the formation of cold lawsonite-blueschists, making the duality of intermediate and high T/P ratios the primary indicator of subduction.
Regional metamorphic rocks serve as monitors of tectonic settings by using thermobaric (T/P) ratios at the metamorphic peak to define thermal gradients.
Pulsating orogenesis describes an orogenic event consisting of several recurring, short-lived metamorphic cycles rather than a single continuous event.
The WDC study provides rare evidence for spatially adjacent paired metamorphic belts, which are seldom preserved in the Archean rock record.

flashcards.q: What are the two primary metamorphic domains analyzed in the Western Dharwar Craton (WDC) study?
flashcards.a: The study analyzes a medium-grade (MG) domain, represented by pelitic schists, and a high-grade (HG) domain, represented by mafic and metasedimentary granulites.

flashcards.q: How is 'paired metamorphism' defined in the context of the Early Earth?
flashcards.a: It refers to the duality of thermal regimes in spatially adjacent domains, specifically one with intermediate T/P (temperature/pressure) gradients and another with high T/P gradients.

flashcards.q: What mineral stability fields distinguish the MG and HG domains in the WDC?
flashcards.a: The medium-grade (MG) domain is characterized by the stability field of kyanite, while the high-grade (HG) domain is characterized by the stability field of sillimanite.

flashcards.q: What are the typical cooling and exhumation rates for the MG domain in the WDC?
flashcards.a: The MG domain experienced relatively fast metamorphic cooling (10-20 °C/Myr) and faster exhumation rates (0.6 to 2 mm/yr).

flashcards.q: How does the crustal residence time of the HG domain compare to the MG domain?
flashcards.a: The HG domain had an extremely long-lived lower-mid-crustal residence of approximately 238 Myrs, whereas the MG domain's residence was relatively short-lived at 10-20 Myrs.

flashcards.q: What tectonic model is proposed to explain the paired metamorphism found in the Western Dharwar Craton?
flashcards.a: The study suggests the 'peel-back convergence' style of plate tectonics, which was operational at the Archean-Proterozoic boundary.

flashcards.q: Define 'pulsating orogenesis' as described in the lecture content.
flashcards.a: It is an orogenesis consisting of several short-lived heating-cooling and burial-exhumation stages as part of multiple metamorphic cycles, each with a distinct P-T path.

flashcards.q: What was the approximate time interval for the coeval metamorphism in both WDC domains?
flashcards.a: The metamorphism occurred between approximately 2.53 and 2.41 Ga during the same orogenic event.

flashcards.q: In Phanerozoic paired metamorphism, what do the contrasting thermal regimes represent?
flashcards.a: They represent spatially adjacent fossil subduction zones (high P/T) and the arc-back-arc systems (low P/T) in the orogenic hinterland.

flashcards.q: What are the two spatially adjacent tectonic domains identified in thermo-mechanical models of peel-back convergence?
flashcards.a: The models identify the thickened crustal zone (TCZ), which corresponds to intermediate T/P, and the peel-off zone (PoZ), which corresponds to high T/P.

flashcards.q: What were the maximum temperatures (TMax) recorded in the HG domain of the WDC?
flashcards.a: The high-grade domain recorded maximum temperatures between 800°C and 870°C.

flashcards.q: Why does the Archean Earth record 'intermediate T/P' rather than 'high P/T' metamorphism like the Phanerozoic?
flashcards.a: The Archean Earth was hotter, which inhibited the formation of cold subduction indicators like lawsonite-blueschists and ultra-high pressure eclogites.

flashcards.q: What type of P-T paths did the medium-grade (MG) domain follow?
flashcards.a: The MG domain followed multiple clockwise (CW) P-T paths representing recurring burial-exhumation and heating-cooling cycles.

mcqs.question: Which mineral stability field is diagnostic of the High-Grade (HG) domain in the Western Dharwar Craton according to the study?
options: A) Kyanite
B) Glaucophane
C) Sillimanite
D) Jadeite

mcqs.question: What significant tectonic transition is hypothesized to have occurred at the Archean-Proterozoic boundary?
options: A) From plume-driven vertical tectonics to asymmetric plate subduction
B) From cold subduction to mantle-driven stagnant lid regime
C) From horizontal plate tectonics to vertical crustal dripping
D) From asymmetric subduction to uniform global cooling

mcqs.question: Despite having uniform burial to lower crustal depths, the MG and HG domains primarily differ in which aspect of their evolution?
options: A) Total depth of burial
B) Thermal (T-t) history and T/P ratios
C) The direction of their P-T paths
D) Initial formation age of the protolith

mcqs.question: How do the exhumation rates of the Medium-Grade (MG) domain compare to the High-Grade (HG) domain?
options: A) The MG domain exhumed slower at approximately 0.1 mm/yr
B) Both domains exhumed at a uniform rate of 1-2 mm/yr
C) The HG domain exhumed ten times faster than the MG domain
D) The MG domain exhumed significantly faster (0.6-2 mm/yr) than the HG domain (~0.1 mm/yr)

mcqs.question: In the context of the study, what is meant by 'pulsating orogenesis'?
options: A) A single, continuous heating event lasting over 500 million years
B) Subduction of cold oceanic crust to depths exceeding 100 km
C) Several short-lived heating-cooling and burial-exhumation stages with distinct P-T paths
D) Vertical movement of crustal blocks driven entirely by mantle plumes

mcqs.question: Which of the following best characterizes the cooling history of the High-Grade (HG) domain?
options: A) Rapid cooling at rates of 10-20 °C/Myr
B) Ultra-slow cooling at approximately 2 °C/Myr
C) Isothermal exhumation followed by rapid quenching
D) Constant temperature residence followed by abrupt burial

mcqs.question: According to the study, the presence of spatially linked paired metamorphism (intermediate T/P and high T/P) is indicative of which process?
options: A) Gravitational instability in greenstone successions
B) One-sided, asymmetric subduction at convergent margins
C) Uniform global warming due to increased mantle radioactivity
D) Symmetrical collision between two equally dense continental plates

mcqs.question: In the 'peel-back convergence' model, how are the Thickened Crustal Zone (TCZ) and Peel-off Zone (PoZ) distinguished by their metamorphic signatures?
options: A) TCZ shows intermediate T/P ratios, while PoZ shows high T/P ratios
B) TCZ exhibits monocyclic evolution while PoZ is always polycyclic
C) TCZ is characterized by low pressure, while PoZ reaches ultra-high pressures
D) TCZ represents the arc system while PoZ represents the subducting oceanic slab

mcqs.question: Why is the traditional Miyashiro-style paired metamorphism (high P/T vs. low P/T) modified when examining Archean rock records?
options: A) Because Archean rocks do not contain kyanite or sillimanite
B) Because the Archean Earth was cooler, preventing the formation of granulites
C) Because the hotter Archean Earth inhibited the formation of cold lawsonite-blueschists and eclogites
D) Because plate tectonics did not exist until the Phanerozoic

mcqs.question: Which set of findings regarding the Medium-Grade (MG) domain supports its classification as having a 'short-lived' crustal residence?
options: A) Residence time of ~238 Myrs and cooling of ~2 °C/Myr
B) Residence time of 10-20 Myrs and cooling of 10-20 °C/Myr
C) Peak temperatures of 870 °C and monocyclic CW P-T paths
D) Stability in the sillimanite field and exhumation of 0.1 mm/yr
